body: claimed: MainSession research agent · 2026-11-13T09:55:34Z · no branch · plan: research

Research answers, read from main (assets/posts/AGENTS.md, crates/post/src/post/{engine,js}.rs, assets/posts/*.cps, crates/app/src/{posting,schema}.rs and commands/post_options.rs, crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_options.rs, crates/app/src/mcp/).

What exists today
- Post options are the `PostOptions` component (threading, skip_stops, per_op, smoothing, end_units) at document level, with a per-setup override (`SetSetupPostOptions`, #389). `posting::options_value` turns it into the JSON the script reads as the global `postOptions`; an option that is off is left out, so output stays byte-identical (the smoothing pattern, #616).
- Both commands are undoable and the UI shows the options in `post_options.rs`. There is no MCP tool for post options at all yet (no `PostOptions` mention under `crates/app/src/mcp/`), so an MCP switch needs the tool itself, not only one more field.
- Every `.cps` has its own `block(words)` and `note(s)`; comment syntax differs (`( )` in Fanuc/Haas/Mazak/Doosan/Tormach/grblHAL/Carvera, `;` in Sinumerik and Heidenhain). Only the LinuxCNC-family posts (tormach, grblhal) have the `ACTIVE` guard that leads a comment starting MSG/DEBUG/PRINT/LOG/PY... with "- ". The engine knows nothing of comment syntax, and no machine file states a line or comment length limit or a program size limit.

Recommended design
1. Where it lives: one new document-level post option `Explain` (default off), with the usual per-setup override, in `PostOptions`. It is published as `postOptions.Explain = true` only when on. Not a per-post property and not a machine setting: it is the operator's choice for one program, like smoothing. Also in the post dialog (document and setup pages) and over MCP.
2. Where the comment is produced: the shared PRELUDE (js.rs) gets one helper, `explain(words)`, that returns the trailing comment for a block from its G/M/T/S/F words, using ONE original wording table (written from RS-274, LinuxCNC docs, and the controls' public manuals) so wording is not copied 15 times and a wording fix lands once. Each post's `block()` calls it and appends the result AFTER the executable words, in the dialect's own syntax. The engine, not each post, applies the guards, so a post cannot forget them: comment text is cleaned to printable ASCII without comment delimiters, the ACTIVE-keyword lead guard is applied for every dialect (harmless elsewhere), and the comment is truncated to the post's `commentMax` so the executable words are never shortened or dropped.
3. Dialect opt-in and refusal: a post declares `explains = "paren"` or `"semi"` (optionally `commentMax`) in its manifest. A post that states none (Heidenhain conversational, anything with no comment form) is refused by name when Explain is on, before any hook runs, the way `programUnits` refuses inch (#902). Never a silent skip.
4. Inert comments, proved: a test posts every golden twice, with and without Explain, strips the trailing comments, and asserts the two programs are byte-identical; plus a test that no comment text begins with an ACTIVE keyword.
5. Detail level (question 6): one comment per block that carries a G/M/T/S word, with modal words explained where they are written (so the same G1 repeated is not re-explained on a bare X/Y/Z continuation block). A change-only mode is not needed because the engine already writes modal words only on change.
6. Program size (question 5): no machine file states a size limit today, so there is nothing to refuse against. Recommendation: no new machine field now; the dialog text says the program gets longer. If a size field is wanted later it is its own issue.

Scope (question 2): the engine pieces plus Tormach/LinuxCNC first (the user's example), then the Fanuc family (Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Doosan), then the rest (Sinumerik, Heidenhain DIN/ISO, grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera, lathes, plasma, wire/sinker). Each is its own PR with goldens.

Wording source (question 4): written fresh from public references only; the table cites its source per entry in a provenance comment. The example text in this issue is a layout illustration, not a wording to copy.

Open for the maintainer (my recommendation in brackets): the exact word table texts and capitalisation of the comments [upper case, as in the example, short, unit named once on the unit word]; whether a default comment width above which the comment is cut should be 60 characters [yes, 60, per-post override via `commentMax`]. Neither blocks the sub-issues.

Sub-issues follow.

Research done; sub-issues filed: #1386 (engine option, explain() helper, refusal), #1387 (Tormach/LinuxCNC), #1388 (Fanuc family), #1389 (remaining dialects), #1390 (post dialog switch and MCP tool). Closed as an umbrella; only the sub-issues are picked for code.
